268. In the explanation of the Aṭṭhānapāḷi, a non-existent basis is 'aṭṭhānaṃ,' or 'aṭṭhānaṃ' means 'there is no basis.' 'Anavakāso' also follows the same principle here. For the conclusion of its meaning is simply the statement, 'This basis does not exist.' Hence it is said: 'ubhayenapī' and so on. 'Yanti' is a singular term in the sense of cause. Here, the meaning of 'hetu' is the meaning of 'kāraṇa,' so he says, 'yanti means by which cause.' Here, by the supreme explanation, the accomplishment of view should be understood, as it is said: 'endowed with the view of the path.' But how is this meaning derived? From the sign; and its sign is the rejection of approaching it as permanent. 'Catubhūmakesu' is said because the formations of the four planes come into the domain of a noble disciple, but not because there is any possibility of approaching them as permanent. For it will be said: 'in the absence of that, however, the formations of the four planes…' and so on. Because volitionally formed formations and formative formations are partial, the term 'in conditioned formations' is used in order to include formations without qualification. However, concerning supramundane formations, he himself will state the reason for their exclusion. This reason does not exist; thus, in approaching them in such a way, there is no 'breaking of the bridge.' 'Tejussadattā' means due to the abundance of the power that dispels defilements. Thus, because of their profundity, they are hard to see and do not become an object for unwholesome states. This, however, is said in the context of the discussion. For in the mental continuities of those whose perversions have not been abandoned, they do not become an object even for wholesome states.

269. Asukhe sukhanti vipallāso ca idha sukhato upagamanassa ṭhānanti dassento “ekanta…pe… attadiṭṭhivasenā”ti padhānadiṭṭhimāha. Gūthanti gūthaṭṭhānaṃ, diṭṭhiyā nibbānassa avisayabhāvo heṭṭhā vutto evāti kasiṇādipaṇṇattisaṅgahatthanti vuttaṃ.

269. Showing that the perversion 'pleasure in what is not pleasure' is here a basis for approaching it as pleasure, he states the principal view: 'ekanta…pe… attadiṭṭhivasenā.' 'Gūthaṃ' means a place of filth. That Nibbāna is not an object for the view has already been stated previously; this is said for the purpose of including concepts such as kasiṇa, etc.

270. Paricchedoti paricchindanaṃ paricchijja tassa gahaṇaṃ. Svāyaṃ yesu niccādito upagamanaṃ sambhavati, tesaṃ vasenayeva kātabboti dassento “sabbavāresu vā”tiādimāha. Sabbavāresūti “niccato upagaccheyyā”tiādinā āgatesu sabbesu suttapadesu. Puthujjano hīti hi-saddo hetuattho. Yasmā yaṃ yaṃ saṅkhāraṃ puthujjano niccādivasena gaṇhāti, taṃ taṃ ariyasāvako aniccādivasena gaṇhanto yāthāvato [M 1.0212] jānanto taṃ gāhaṃ taṃ diṭṭhiṃ vissajjeti, tasmā yattha [V 1.0198] gāho, tattha vissajjanāti catubhūmakasaṅkhārā idha saṅkhāraggahaṇena na gayhantīti attho.

270. 'Paricchedo' means delimitation, having delimited, the grasping of it. Showing that this should be done only with respect to those things where approaching as permanent, etc., is possible, he said, 'sabbavāresu vā,' and so on. 'Sabbavāresu' refers to all the text passages in the suttas beginning with 'niccato upagaccheyyā,' and so on. In 'puthujjano hi,' the word 'hi' has the meaning of reason. Because whatever formation the ordinary person grasps as permanent, etc., the noble disciple, knowing it as it actually is while grasping it as impermanent, etc., abandons that grasping and that view. Therefore, 'where there is grasping, there is abandoning.' The meaning is that the formations pertaining to the four planes are not included here by the term 'formations.'

271. Puttasambandhena mātupitusamaññā dattakittimādivasenapi puttavohāro loke dissati, so ca kho pariyāyenāti nippariyāyena siddhaṃ taṃ dassetuṃ – “janikāva mātā, janakova pitā”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā ānantariyakammassa adhippetattā “manussabhūtova khīṇāsavo arahāti adhippeto”ti vuttaṃ. “Aṭṭhānameta”ntiādinā “mātuādīnaṃyeva jīvitā voropane ariyasāvakassa abhabbabhāvadassanato tadaññaṃ ariyasāvako jīvitā voropetīti idaṃ atthato āpannamevā”ti maññamāno vadati – “kiṃ pana ariyasāvako aññaṃ jīvitā voropeyyā”ti? “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso, yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti vacanato “etampi aṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Tenevāha – “sace hī”tiādi. Evaṃ sante kasmā “mātara”ntiādinā visesetvā vuttanti āha – “puthujjanabhāvassa panā”tiādi. Tattha baladīpanatthanti saddhādibalasamannāgamadīpanatthaṃ. Ariyamaggenāgatasaddhādhibalavasena hi ariyasāvako tādisaṃ sāvajjaṃ na karoti.

271. Through the bond of sonship, the terms mother and father are given. In the world, the designation of son is seen even through adoption and the like, but that is only in a figurative sense. To show what is established in the literal sense, it is said: 'The birth-giver is the mother, the begetter is the father.' Similarly, because an act with immediate result is intended, it is said: 'An arahant who is a human being with cankers destroyed is intended.' Thinking that since the statement 'Aṭṭhānametaṃ' and so forth shows the incapability of a noble disciple to deprive their mother or the like of life, a noble disciple might deprive another of life, one might ask: 'But could a noble disciple deprive another of life?' From the statement, 'This is impossible, it is no occasion, that a person accomplished in view would intentionally deprive a living being of life—this basis does not exist,' it is said: 'This too is impossible.' Therefore, he says: 'sace hi' and so on. Given this, why is it specified with 'mother,' and so forth? He says: 'puthujjanabhāvassa panā' and so on. There, 'for the sake of illustrating strength' means for the sake of illustrating the possession of the strength of faith and other faculties. For it is through the strength of faith and other faculties, arrived at by the noble path, that a noble disciple does not commit such a blameworthy act.

275. Pañcahi kāraṇehīti idamettha nipphādakāni tesaṃ pubbabhāgiyāni ca kāraṇāni kāraṇabhāvasāmaññena ekajjhaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ, na pana sabbesaṃ samānayogakkhamattā. Ākārehīti kāraṇehi. Anussāvanenāti anurūpaṃ sāvanena. Bhedassa anurūpaṃ yathā bhedo hoti, evaṃ bhinditabbānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ attano vacanassa sāvanena viññāpanena. Tenāha – “nanu tumhe”tiādi. Kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvāti etena pākaṭaṃ katvā bhedakaravatthudīpanaṃ vohāro, tattha attano nicchitamatthaṃ rahassavasena viññāpanaṃ anussāvananti dasseti.

275. 'By five causes'—this is said here having taken together, under the general term 'causes,' the productive causes and their preliminary conditions, but not because all have equal capacity for application. 'Ākārehi' means by causes. 'Anussāvanena' means by a suitable announcement. It means by making the monks who are to be split hear one's own word, by informing them, in a way suitable for schism, so that a schism occurs. Hence it is said: 'nanu tumhe' and so on. By this 'having made a verbal split at the root of the ear,' he shows that making manifest the matter that causes the split is the 'declaration' (vohāro), whereas informing them of one's own decided opinion in secret is the 'announcement' (anussāvana).

Kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇanti tehi saṅghabhedasiddhito vuttaṃ, itare pana tesaṃ sambhārabhūtā. Tenāha – “vohārā”tiādi. Tatthāti voharaṇe. Cutianantaraṃ phalaṃ anantaraṃ nāma, tasmiṃ anantare niyuttāni, tannibbattanena anantarakaraṇasīlāni, anantarappayojanāni cāti ānantariyāni, tāni eva kammānīti ānantariyakammāni.

It is said that 'the act itself or the proclamation is the standard' because the schism of the Sangha is accomplished by these, while the others are their supporting factors. Hence it is said: 'vohārā' and so on. 'Tattha' means in the declaration. The fruit immediately following passing away is called 'immediate'; those connected with that immediate result, producing it, having the nature of causing an immediate result, and having an immediate purpose—these are the 'immediate actions.' These very actions are called 'acts with immediate result'.

Kammatoti [M 1.0213] “evaṃ ānantariyakammaṃ hoti, evaṃ ānantariyakammasadisa”nti evaṃ kammavibhāgato. Dvāratoti kāyadvārato. Kappaṭṭhitiyatoti “idaṃ kappaṭṭhitiyavipākaṃ, idaṃ na kappaṭṭhitiyavipāka”nti evaṃ kappaṭṭhitiyavibhāgato. Pākasādhāraṇādīhīti “idamettha vipaccati, idaṃ [V 1.0199] na vipaccatī”ti vipaccanavibhāgato, gahaṭṭhapabbajitānaṃ sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇato, ādi-saddena vedanādivibhāgato ca.

Regarding kamma, it is classified thus: 'There is kamma with immediate result, and there is kamma similar to kamma with immediate result.' Regarding the door, it is from the body-door. Regarding the duration of an aeon, it is classified thus: 'This has a result lasting an aeon, this does not have a result lasting an aeon.' By way of commonality of ripening, etc., it is classified by ripening thus: 'This ripens here, this does not ripen here,' and by what is common and uncommon to householders and renunciants, and by the word 'etc.' by way of the classification of feeling, and so on.

Kammato tāva vinicchayo vuccatīti sambandho. Yasmā manussattabhāve ṭhitasseva kusaladhammānaṃ tikkhavisadabhāvāpatti, yathā tiṇṇaṃ bodhisattānaṃ bodhittayanibbattiyaṃ, evaṃ manussabhāve ṭhitasseva edisānaṃ akusaladhammānampi tikkhavisadabhāvāpattīti āha – “manussabhūtassevā”ti. Pākatikamanussānampi ca kusaladhammānaṃ visesappatti vimānavatthuaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Yathāvutto ca attho samānajātiyassa vikopane garutaro, na tathā vijātiyassāti vuttaṃ – “manussabhūtaṃ mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā”ti. Liṅgaparivatte ca so eva ekakammanibbatto bhavaṅgappabandho jīvitindriyapabandho ca, na aññoti āha – “api parivattaliṅga”nti. Arahattaṃ pattepi eseva nayo. Tassa vipākantiādi kammassa ānantariyabhāvasamatthanaṃ. Catukkoṭiyañcettha sambhavati. Tattha paṭhamā koṭi dassitā, itarāsu visaṅketabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ – “yo panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yadipi tattha visaṅketo, kammaṃ pana garutaraṃ ānantariyasadisaṃ bhāyitabbanti āha – “bhāriyaṃ…pe… tiṭṭhatī”ti. Ayaṃ pañhoti ñāpanicchānibbattā kathā.

The connection is that the discrimination of kamma is first mentioned. Because even while existing in the human state, the attainment of sharp and clear wholesome qualities is possible, just as the three Bodhisattas gave rise to the threefold enlightenment while in the human state. Similarly, even while existing in the human state, such sharp and clear unwholesome qualities can arise—thus it is said, 'even while being human.' Moreover, the attainment of excellence in wholesome qualities by ordinary humans should be understood in the way explained in the commentary on the Vimānavatthu. And the meaning as stated is weightier when disrupting one of the same kind, not so when disrupting one of a different kind—thus it is said, 'a human mother or father.' Regarding the transformation of gender, that very same stream of bhavaṅga and stream of the life-faculty is produced by a single kamma, not another. Hence it is said, 'even if the gender changes.' The same principle applies even when one attains arahantship. The phrase 'its result' and so on serves to establish the immediacy of the kamma. Here, a fourfold classification is possible. The first case is shown, and to indicate the absence of confusion in the others, it is said, 'but whoever' and so on. Even where there is no confusion, the kamma should still be regarded as weighty, similar to an immediate kamma—thus it is said, 'heavy... persists.' This is a question—a discourse born from the desire to explain.

Abhisandhināti adhippāyena. Ānantariyaṃ phusatīti maraṇādhippāyeneva ānantariyavatthuno vikopitattā vuttaṃ. Ānantariyaṃ na phusatīti ānantariyavatthuabhāvato ānantariyaṃ na hoti. Sabbattha hi purimaṃ abhisandhicittaṃ appamāṇaṃ, vadhakacittaṃ pana tadārammaṇaṃ jīvitindriyañca ānantariyabhāve pamāṇanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saṅgāmacatukkaṃ sampattavasena yojetabbaṃ. Yo hi parasenāya aññañca yodhaṃ pitarañca kammaṃ karonte disvā yodhassa usuṃ khipati “etaṃ vijjhitvā mama pitaraṃ vijjhissatī”ti, yathādhippāyaṃ gate pitughātako hoti. “Yodhe viddhe mama pitā palāyissatī”ti khipati, usuṃ ayathādhippāyaṃ gantvā pitaraṃ māreti, vohāravasena pitughātakoti vuccati, ānantariyaṃ pana natthīti. Coracatukkaṃ pana yo “coraṃ māressāmī”ti [M 1.0214] coravesena gacchantaṃ pitaraṃ māreti, ānantariyaṃ phusatītiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Tenevāti teneva payogena. Arahantaghātako hotiyevāti arahato māritattā vuttaṃ, puthujjanasseva taṃ dinnaṃ hotīti etthāyamadhippāyo – yathā vadhakacetanā paccuppannārammaṇāpi pabandhavicchedanavasena jīvitindriyaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattati, na evaṃ cāgacetanā. Sā hi cajitabbavatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cajanamattameva hoti, aññasantakabhāvakaraṇañca tassa cajanaṃ, tasmā yassa taṃ santakaṃ kataṃ, tasseva dinnaṃ hotīti.

'Abhisandhinā' means 'with intention.' 'Ānantariyaṃ phusati' is said because the object of an immediate deed is disrupted with the intention to kill. 'Ānantariyaṃ na phusati' means there is no immediate deed because the object for it does not exist. For in all cases, the initial thought of resolve is immeasurable, but the killer's thought, taking that as its object, and the life faculty—these are to be seen as the measure for the state of an immediate deed. The fourfold battle scenario should be applied based on success. For instance, if someone, seeing another warrior and his own father engaged in battle, throws a spear thinking, 'Having pierced this one, I will pierce my father,' and it proceeds as intended, he becomes a father-killer. If he throws the spear thinking, 'When the warrior is pierced, my father will flee,' but the spear goes contrary to intention and kills his father, he is called a father-killer in conventional speech, but there is no immediate deed. The fourfold thief scenario should be applied similarly: if one kills his father, who is going about in the guise of a thief, while intending, 'I will kill the thief,' an immediate deed is incurred. 'Teneva' means 'by that very effort.' 'Arahantaghātako hotiyeva' is said because an arahant has been killed. The intention here in 'it is given only to a worldling' is this: just as the killer's volition, even when taking a present object, occurs by severing the continuity of life, taking the life faculty as its object, it is not so with the volition of giving. For the volition of giving takes the object to be relinquished and merely effects the relinquishment, and the act of relinquishing makes it belong to another. Therefore, it is given only to the one to whom that possession is made.

Lohitaṃ [V 1.0200] samosaratīti abhighātena pakuppamānaṃ sañcitaṃ hoti. Mahantataranti garutaraṃ. Sarīrappaṭijaggane viyāti satthurūpakāyappaṭijaggane viya.

'Lohitaṃ samosarati' means that the blood, agitated by impact, accumulates. 'Mahantataraṃ' means 'heavier.' 'Sarīrappaṭijaggane viya' means 'like the care of the Teacher's physical body.'

Asannipatiteti idaṃ sāmaggiyadīpanaṃ. Bhedo ca hotīti saṅghassa bhedo ca hoti. Vaṭṭatīti saññāyāti “īdisaṃ karaṇaṃ saṅghabhedāya na hotī”ti saññāya. Tathā navato ūnaparisāyāti navato ūnaparisāya karontassa tathāti yojetabbaṃ. Tathāti ca iminā “na ānantariyakamma”nti imaṃ ākaḍḍhati, na pana “bhedova hotī”ti idaṃ. Heṭṭhimantena hi navannameva vasena saṅghabhedo. Dhammavādino anavajjāti yathādhammaṃ anavaṭṭhānato. Saṅghabhedassa pubbabhāgo saṅgharāji.

'Asannipatite'—this is an elucidation of harmony. 'Bhedo ca hoti' means there is indeed a schism in the Saṅgha. 'Vaṭṭati' is by the perception that 'such an action does not lead to schism in the Saṅgha.' Similarly, 'with an assembly of less than nine' means that for one acting with an assembly of less than nine, 'thus' should be connected. And by 'thus,' it draws in 'not an action with immediate result,' but not 'there is indeed schism.' For by the lower limit, schism arises only by way of nine monks. 'Speakers of the Dhamma are blameless' because of not standing firm in what is contrary to the Dhamma. The precursor to schism is the line of division in the Saṅgha.

Kāyadvārameva pūrenti kāyakammabhāveneva lakkhitabbato. Saṇṭhahantehi kappe…pe… muccatīti idaṃ kappaṭṭhakathāya (kathā. 654 ādayo) na sameti. Tattha hi aṭṭhakathāya (kathā. aṭṭha. 654-657) vuttaṃ – “āpāyikoti idaṃ suttaṃ yaṃ so ekaṃ kappaṃ asītibhāge katvā tato ekabhāgamattaṃ kālaṃ tiṭṭheyya, taṃ āyukappaṃ sandhāya vutta”nti. Kappavināseyevāti ca āyukappavināse evāti atthe sati natthi virodho. Ettha ca saṇṭhahanteti idampi “sveva vinassissatī”ti viya abhūtaparikappavasena vuttaṃ. Ekadivasameva niraye paccati, tato paraṃ kappābhāve āyukappassapi abhāvatoti avirodhato atthayojanā daṭṭhabbā. Sesānīti saṅghabhedato aññāni ānantariyakammāni.

They fulfill only the body-door, as they are to be characterized by their very nature as bodily action. 'When the aeon endures... is released'—this does not agree with the commentary on the aeon (Kathāvatthu 654 onwards). There, the commentary (Kathāvatthu-aṭṭhakathā 654-657) states: ''Destined for the woeful state'—this sutta refers to one who, having divided one aeon into eighty parts, would remain for only one part of that time. This was said with reference to the lifespan-aeon.' And 'at the destruction of an aeon' means 'at the destruction of a lifespan-aeon,' so there is no contradiction in the meaning. Here, 'when the aeon endures' is also said by way of a false supposition, like 'it will perish tomorrow.' He is tormented in hell for only one day, and after that, since there is no aeon, there is also no lifespan-aeon—thus, the application of the meaning should be seen as being without contradiction. 'The rest' means the other deeds with immediate result, apart from schism in the Saṅgha.

Yadi tāni ahosikammasaṅkhaṃ gacchanti, evaṃ sati kathaṃ nesaṃ ānantariyatā cutianantaraṃ vipākadānābhāvato. Atha sati phaladāne cutianantaro [M 1.0215] eva etesaṃ phalakālo, na aññoti phalakālaniyamena niyatatā icchitā, na phaladānaniyamena. Evampi niyataphalakālānaṃ aññesampi upapajjavedanīyānaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyānañca niyatatā āpajjeyya, tasmā vipākadhammadhammānaṃ paccayantaravikalatādīhi avipaccamānānampi attano sabhāvena vipākadhammatā viya balavatā ānantariyena vipāke dinne avipaccamānānampi ānantariyānaṃ phaladāne niyatasabhāvā ānantariyasabhāvā ca pavattīti attano sabhāvena phaladānaniyameneva niyatā ānantariyatā ca veditabbā. Avassañca ānantariyasabhāvā tato eva niyatasabhāvā ca tesaṃ pavattīti sampaṭicchitabbametaṃ, aññassa balavato ānantariyassa abhāve sati cutianantaraṃ ekantena phaladānato.

If they are counted as ineffective deeds, then how can their immediacy be explained, since they do not yield results immediately after death? But if they do yield results, then the time for their fruition is immediately after death, not at another time—their certainty is desired in terms of the time of fruition, not in terms of the certainty of yielding results. Even so, this would apply to other deeds with fixed fruition times, such as those to be experienced in the next life or in this very life. Therefore, just as the nature of result-bearing phenomena, even when not ripening due to a deficiency of intervening conditions, still inherently possesses the capacity to yield results, so too, when a powerful immediate deed has given its result, the fixed and immediate nature of other such deeds, even when not ripening, proceeds in the yielding of a result; thus, their immediacy should be understood as being fixed by the very rule of yielding a result by its own nature. And it must be accepted that their immediacy, and thus their fixed nature, proceeds from that very fact, since, in the absence of any other stronger immediate deed, they yield results exclusively immediately after death.

Nanu [V 1.0201] evaṃ aññesampi upapajjavedanīyānaṃ aññasmiṃ vipākadāyake asati cutianantarameva ekantena phaladānato niyatasabhāvā ānantariyasabhāvā ca pavatti āpajjatīti? Nāpajjati asamānajātikena cetopaṇidhivasena upaghātakena ca nivattetabbavipākattā anantare ekantaphaladāyakattābhāvā, na pana ānantariyānaṃ paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ dutiyajjhānādīni viya asamānajātikaṃ phalanivattakaṃ atthi sabbānantariyānaṃ avīciphalattā, na ca heṭṭhūpapattiṃ icchato sīlavato cetopaṇidhi viya uparūpapattijanakakammaphalaṃ ānantariyaphalaṃ nivattetuṃ samattho cetopaṇidhi atthi anicchantasseva avīcipātanato, na ca ānantariyopaghātakaṃ kiñci kammaṃ atthi, tasmā tesaṃyeva anantare ekantavipākajanakasabhāvā pavattīti. Anekāni ca ānantariyāni katāni ekantena vipāke niyatasabhāvattā uparatāvipaccanasabhāvāsaṅkattā nicchitāni sabhāvato niyatāneva. Tesu pana samānasabhāvesu ekena vipāke dinne itarāni attanā kattabbakiccassa teneva katattā na dutiyaṃ tatiyampi ca paṭisandhiṃ karonti, na samatthatāvighātattāti natthi tesaṃ ānantariyakatānivatti, garugarutarabhāvo pana tesaṃ labbhatevāti saṅghabhedassa siyā garutarabhāvoti “yena…pe… vipaccatī”ti āha. Ekassa pana aññāni upatthambhakāni hontīti daṭṭhabbāni. Paṭisandhivasena vipaccatīti vacanena itaresaṃ pavattivipākadāyitā anuññātā viya dissati. No vā tathā sīlavatīti yathā pitā sīlavā, tathā sīlavatī [M 1.0216] no vā hotīti yojanā. Sace mātā sīlavatī, mātughāto paṭisandhivasena vipaccatīti yojanā.

But if this is so, then for other kammas to be experienced in the next existence, when there is no other result-giving kamma, would not an occurrence of a fixed and immediately resultant nature arise, giving its fruit invariably immediately after death? It does not arise, because their result can be averted by a mental aspiration of a different kind and by a destructive kamma, and because they do not have the nature of invariably giving fruit immediately. However, for the immediately resultant kammas, there is no result-averting factor of a different kind, as the second jhāna and so on are for the first jhāna and so on, since all immediately resultant kammas have the Avīci hell as their result. Nor is there any mental aspiration capable of averting the result of an immediately resultant kamma, like the aspiration of a virtuous person who wishes for a lower rebirth averting the result of a kamma that generates a higher rebirth, since the immediately resultant kamma causes rebirth in Avīci even if one does not wish for it. Moreover, there is no kamma capable of obstructing an immediately resultant kamma. Therefore, their occurrence is immediate and invariably productive of results. Furthermore, when many immediately resultant kammas have been committed, because they have a fixed nature in invariably giving a result and because they have the nature of ceasing to ripen once ripened, they are by nature determined and certain. Among those of a similar nature, when one has given its result, the others do not produce a second or a third rebirth-linking, because the deed to be done by them has been done by that very one; this is not due to an obstruction of their capacity. Thus, there is no averting of the committed immediately resultant kammas. However, a state of being heavier or heaviest is found among them, so schism in the Sangha may be the heaviest, which is why it is said, 'by which... and so on... it ripens'. But it should be understood that for one, the others serve as supporting conditions. The statement 'it ripens by way of rebirth-linking' seems to imply that the others are permitted to give results during the course of existence. Or, 'not so virtuous' is to be construed as: 'Just as the father is virtuous, is she virtuous or not?' If the mother is virtuous, then matricide ripens by way of rebirth-linking—this is the connection.

Pakatattoti anukkhitto. Samānasaṃvāsakoti apārājiko. Samānasīmāyanti ekasīmāyaṃ.

Pakatatta means 'not suspended'. Samānasaṃvāsaka means 'one who has not committed an offense of defeat'. Samānasīmāyaṃ means 'within a single boundary'.

276. Satthu kiccaṃ kātuṃ asamatthoti yaṃ satthārā kātabbakiccaṃ anusāsanādi, naṃ kātuṃ asamatthoti bhagavantaṃ paccakkhāya. Aññaṃ titthakaranti aññaṃ satthāraṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ –

276. Unable to perform the Teacher's duty means unable to perform the duty to be done by the Teacher, such as instruction, thus rejecting the Blessed One. Aññaṃ titthakaraṃ means 'another sectarian teacher'. For it has been said:

“Titthaṃ jānitabbaṃ, titthakaro jānitabbo, titthiyā jānitabbā, titthiyasāvakā jānitabbā. Tattha titthaṃ nāma dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo. Ettha hi satthā taranti uplavanti ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti, tasmā titthanti vuccanti. Tādisānaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ uppādetā titthakaro nāma pūraṇakassapādiko. Tassa laddhiṃ gahetvā pabbajitā titthiyā nāma. Te hi titthe jātāti titthiyā. Yathāvuttaṃ vā diṭṭhigatasaṅkhātaṃ titthaṃ etesaṃ atthīti titthikā[V 1.0202], titthikā eva titthiyā. Tesaṃ paccayadāyakā titthiyasāvakāti veditabbā”ti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.140).

'A ford should be understood, a ford-maker should be understood, sectarians should be understood, and sectarian disciples should be understood. Here, a 'ford' means the sixty-two views. For in this, teachers cross over, float, and repeatedly emerge and submerge; therefore, it is called a ford. The originator of such views is called a ford-maker, such as Pūraṇa Kassapa and others. Those who have gone forth having adopted his doctrine are called sectarians. For they are born in a ford, thus they are 'sectarians.' Or, as stated, a 'ford' is a category of views; since they have this, they are 'titthikā,' and 'titthikā' is just 'titthiyā.' Their supporters who provide requisites are to be understood as sectarian disciples.' (MA.i.140)

277. Abhijātiādīsu pakampanadevatūpasaṅkamanādinā jātacakkavāḷena samānayogakkhamaṃ dasasahassaparimāṇaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ jātikhettaṃ. Saraseneva āṇāpavattanaṭṭhānaṃ āṇākhettaṃ. Visayabhūtaṃ ṭhānaṃ visayakhettaṃ. Dasasahassī lokadhātūti imāya lokadhātuyā saddhiṃ imaṃ lokadhātuṃ parivāretvā ṭhitā dasasahassī lokadhātu. Tattakānaṃyeva jātikhettabhāvo dhammatāvasena veditabbo. “Pariggahavasenā”ti keci, “sabbesaṃyeva buddhānaṃ tattakaṃyeva jātikhettaṃ tannivāsīnaṃyeva devatānaṃ dhammābhisamayo”ti ca vadanti. Mātukucchi okkamanakālādīnaṃ channaṃ eva gahaṇaṃ nidassanamattaṃ mahābhinīhārādikālepi tassa pakampanassa labbhanato. Āṇākhettaṃ nāma yaṃ ekajjhaṃ saṃvaṭṭati vivaṭṭati ca, āṇā pavattati āṇāya tannivāsidevatānaṃ sirasā sampaṭicchanena, tañca kho kevalaṃ buddhānaṃ ānubhāveneva, na adhippāyavasena. Adhippāyavasena [M 1.0217] pana “yāvatā vā pana ākaṅkheyyā”ti (a. ni. 3.81) vacanato tato parampi āṇā vatteyyeva.

277. In the case of birth and so on, the field of birth (jātikhetta) is a ten-thousandfold world-system, which is capable of the same application as the world-system of birth, with the trembling, the approaching of deities, and so on. The field of command (āṇākhetta) is the place where the command operates by its own nature. The field of range (visayakhetta) is the place that is its object. The ten-thousandfold world-system means the ten thousand world-systems standing surrounding this world-system, together with this world-system. That the field of birth is of that extent should be understood as due to the nature of things. Some say, 'By way of encompassing power,' and 'the field of birth is the same for all Buddhas, and the Dhamma-realization is only for the deities dwelling therein.' The taking of the six instances, such as the time of entering the mother's womb, is merely illustrative, since that trembling is obtainable even at the time of the Great Resolve, and so on. The field of command is that which contracts and expands together, where the command operates through the deities dwelling therein accepting it with their heads, and that is solely by the Buddha's power, not by way of intention. However, by way of intention, the command could indeed operate even beyond that, since it is said, 'As far as one might desire' (AN 3.81).

Na uppajjantīti pana atthīti “na me ācariyo atthi, sadiso me na vijjatī”tiādiṃ (ma. ni. 1.285; mahāva. 11; kathā. 405) imissā lokadhātuyā ṭhatvā vadantena bhagavatā “kiṃ panāvuso, sāriputta, atthetarahi aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā samasamā sambodhiyanti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘no’ti vadeyya”nti (dī. ni. 3.161) vatvā tassa kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ – “aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyu”nti imaṃ suttaṃ (a. ni. 1.277; vibha. 809; ma. ni. 3.129; mi. pa. 5.1.1) āharantena dhammasenāpatinā ca buddhakhettabhūtaṃ imaṃ lokadhātuṃ ṭhapetvā aññattha anuppatti vuttā hotīti adhippāyo.

‘Yet, is it the case that they do not arise?’—The intention is this: by the Blessed One, who, standing in this world-system, declared, ‘I have no teacher, nor is there anyone like me’ (MN 1.285; Vin.i.11; Kv.405), and by the General of the Dhamma, who, to show the reason for this, said, ‘But, friend Sāriputta, if I were asked, “Are there now any other ascetics or brahmins equal to the Blessed One in supreme enlightenment?” I would say, “No, venerable sir”’ (DN 3.161), and brought forth this sutta: ‘This is impossible, there is no chance that two arahants, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, could arise in one world-system, one not preceding, one not following’ (AN 1.277; Vibh.809; MN 3.129; Miln.5.1.1)—the non-arising of another is stated with respect to this world-system, which is the Buddha-field.

Ekatoti saha, ekasmiṃ kāleti attho, so pana kālo kathaṃ paricchinnoti carimabhave paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya yāva dhātuparinibbānāti dassento, “tatthā”tiādimāha. Anacchariyattāti dvīsupi uppajjamānesu acchariyattābhāvatoti attho. Dvīsupi uppajjamānesu anacchariyatā, kimaṅgaṃ pana bahūsūti dassento, “yadi cā”tiādimāha. Buddhā nāma majjhe bhinnasuvaṇṇaṃ viya ekasadisāti tesaṃ desanāpi ekarasā ekadhāti āha – “desanāya ca visesābhāvato”ti[V 1.0203]. Etenapi anacchariyattameva sādheti. Vivādabhāvatoti etena vivādābhāvatthaṃ dve buddhā ekato na uppajjantīti dasseti. Etaṃ kāraṇanti etaṃ anacchariyatādikāraṇaṃ. Tatthāti milindapañhe.

'At one time' means together, at a single time. But how is that time defined? Showing that it starts from the moment of rebirth-linking in the final existence up until the final parinibbāna of the elements, he said, 'at that time,' and so on. 'Not astonishing' means because there is no astonishment even when two arise. Showing that if there is no astonishment when two arise, how much more so when many arise, he said, 'if even,' and so on. Buddhas are alike, like a single piece of gold broken in the middle. He said that their teaching is of one taste, one nature: 'because there is no distinction in their teaching.' By this too, he establishes the absence of astonishment. 'Because of the absence of dispute'—by this he indicates that two Buddhas do not arise simultaneously in order to prevent disputes. 'This is the reason'—this refers to the reason of non-astonishment and so on. 'In that' refers to the Milindapañha.

Ekaṃ eva buddhaṃ dhāretīti ekabuddhadhāraṇī. Etena evaṃsabhāvā ete buddhaguṇā, yena dutiyabuddhaguṇe dhāretuṃ asamatthā ayaṃ lokadhātūti dasseti. Paccayavisesanipphannānañhi guṇadhammānaṃ bhāriyo viseso mahāpathaviyāpi dussahoti sakkā viññātuṃ. Tathā hi abhisambodhisamaye upagatassa lokanāthassa guṇabhāraṃ bodhirukkhassa tīsupi disāsu mahāpathavī sandhāretuṃ nāsakkhi. Tasmā “na dhāreyyā”ti vatvā tameva adhāraṇaṃ pariyāyantarehi pakāsento “caleyyā”tiādimāha. Tattha caleyyāti paripphandeyya. Kampeyyāti pavedheyya[M 1.0218]. Nameyyāti ekapassena nameyya. Onameyyāti osīdeyya. Vinameyyāti vividhaṃ ito cito ca nameyya. Vikireyyāti vātena thusamuṭṭhi viya vippakireyya. Vidhameyyāti vinasseyya. Viddhaṃseyyāti sabbaso viddhastā bhaveyya. Tathābhūtā ca na katthaci tiṭṭheyyāti āha – “na ṭhānamupagaccheyyā”ti.

It upholds only one Buddha—this is the 'ekabuddhadhāraṇī.' By this, it shows that the Buddha-qualities are of such a nature that this world-system is incapable of upholding the qualities of a second Buddha. For it can be understood that the great weight of virtuous qualities, produced by specific conditions, is unbearable even for the great earth. Indeed, at the time of his supreme enlightenment, the great earth could not bear the weight of the Lord of the World's virtues in all three directions around the Bodhi tree. Therefore, having said, 'It would not uphold,' he then reveals this inability to bear in various ways, stating, 'It would shake,' and so on. Here, 'it would shake' means it would quiver. 'It would quake' means it would be agitated. 'It would bend' means it would incline to one side. 'It would sink' means it would subside. 'It would twist' means it would bend in various ways here and there. 'It would scatter' means it would be scattered like a handful of chaff by the wind. 'It would be destroyed' means it would perish. 'It would be shattered' means it would be completely broken apart. And being in such a state, it would find no place to stand—thus it is said, 'It would find no footing.'

Idāni tattha nidassanaṃ dassento, “yathā, mahārājā”tiādimāha. Tattha eke puriseti ekasmiṃ purise. Samupādikāti samaṃ uddhaṃ pajjati pavattatīti samupādikā, udakassa upari samaṃ gāminīti attho. “Samuppādikā”tipi paṭhanti, ayamevattho. Vaṇṇenāti saṇṭhānena. Pamāṇenāti ārohena. Kisathūlenāti kisathūlabhāvena, pariṇāhenāti attho. Dvinnampīti dvepi, dvinnampi vā sarīrabhāraṃ.

Now, giving an illustration there, he said, 'Just as, great king,' and so on. Here, 'in one man' means in a single man. 'Samupādikā' means that which goes evenly upward, which proceeds uniformly; that is, moving evenly on the surface of the water. Some read it as 'samuppādikā,' but this is the same meaning. 'By appearance' means by shape. 'By measure' means by height. 'By thinness or thickness' means by the state of being thin or thick; that is, by circumference. 'Of both' means both, or the bodily burden of both.

Chādentanti rocentaṃ ruciṃ uppādentaṃ. Tandikatoti tena bhojanena tandibhūto. Anonamitadaṇḍajātoti yāvadatthaṃ bhojanena onamituṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya anonamanadaṇḍo viya jāto. Sakiṃ bhutto vameyyāti ekampi ālopaṃ ajjhoharitvā vameyyāti attho.

'Chādentaṃ' means pleasing, arousing desire. 'Tandikato' means having become weary from that food. 'Anonamitadaṇḍajāto' means having become like an unbending staff from being unable to bend down as much as desired for the food. 'Sakiṃ bhutto vameyya' means that having swallowed even a single morsel, one would vomit.

Atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti dhammena nāma pathavī tiṭṭheyya. Sā kiṃ teneva calati vinassatīti adhippāyena pucchati. Puna thero “ratanaṃ nāma loke kuṭumbaṃ sandhārentaṃ abhimatañca lokena attano garusabhāvatāya sakaṭabhaṅgassa kāraṇaṃ atibhārabhūtaṃ diṭṭhaṃ. Evaṃ dhammo ca hitasukhavisesehi taṃsamaṅgīnaṃ dhārento abhimato ca viññūnaṃ gambhīrappameyyabhāvena garusabhāvattā atibhārabhūto pathavīcalanassa kāraṇaṃ hotī”ti dassento, “idha, mahārāja, dve sakaṭā”tiādimāha[V 1.0204]. Eteneva tathāgatassa mātukucchiokkamanādikāle pathavīkampanakāraṇaṃ saṃvaṇṇitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ekassāti ekasmā, ekassa vā sakaṭassa ratanaṃ, tasmā sakaṭā gahetvāti attho.

“The earth trembles under the excessive weight of the Dhamma”—if so, the earth should stand firm by the Dhamma. Does it then tremble and perish because of that? This is the implied question. Again, the elder explains: “In the world, a jewel, which maintains a household and is esteemed by the world, is seen as an excessive burden due to its heavy nature, causing the cart to break. Similarly, the Dhamma, which maintains those endowed with it with special welfare and happiness, and is esteemed by the wise, becomes an excessive burden due to its heavy nature on account of its profundity and immeasurability, causing the earth to tremble.” To illustrate this, he says, “Here, great king, are two carts,” and so on. By this, it should be understood that the cause of the earth’s trembling at the time of the Tathāgata’s descent into his mother’s womb and other such occasions is described. 'Ekassa' means from one, or the jewel of one cart; therefore, the meaning is “taking it from that cart.”

Osāritanti uccāritaṃ, vuttanti attho. Aggoti sabbasattehi aggo. Jeṭṭhoti vuddhataro. Seṭṭhoti pasatthataro. Visiṭṭhehi sīlādīhi guṇehi samannāgatattā visiṭṭho. Uggatatamoti uttamo. Pavaroti [M 1.0219] tasseva vevacanaṃ. Natthi etassa samoti asamo. Asamā pubbabuddhā, tehi samoti asamasamo. Natthi etassa paṭisamo paṭipuggaloti appaṭisamo. Natthi etassa paṭibhāgoti appaṭibhāgo. Natthi etassa paṭipuggaloti appaṭipuggalo.

'Osāritaṃ' means uttered, that is to say, spoken. 'Agga' means foremost among all beings. 'Jeṭṭha' means older, senior. 'Seṭṭha' means most praised. 'Visiṭṭha' means distinguished because he is endowed with excellent qualities such as virtue. 'Uggatatama' means highest, supreme. 'Pavara' is a synonym for that same word. 'Asama' means without equal, for there is no equal to him. 'Asamasama' means equal to the Unequalled, that is, the past Buddhas. 'Appaṭisama' means without a counterpart, for there is no person who is his match. 'Appaṭibhāga' means without a counterpart, for there is no counterpart to him. 'Appaṭipuggala' means without a counterpart person, for there is no person who is his counterpart.

Sabhāvapakatikāti sabhāvabhūtā akittimā pakati. Kāraṇamahantattāti kāraṇānaṃ mahantatāya, mahantehi buddhakaradhammehi pāramisaṅkhātehi kāraṇehi buddhaguṇānaṃ nibbattitoti vuttaṃ hoti. Pathavīādīni mahantāni vatthūni, mahantā cakkavāḷādayo attano attano visaye ekekāva, evaṃ sammāsambuddhopi mahanto attano visaye eko eva. Ko ca tassa visayo? Buddhabhūmi, yāvatakaṃ vā ñeyyaṃ. “Ākāso viya anantavisayo bhagavā eko eva hotī”ti vadanto paracakkavāḷesupi dutiyassa buddhassa abhāvaṃ dasseti.

'Sabhāvapakatika' means the inherent, unartificial nature. 'Kāraṇamahantattā' means due to the greatness of the causes—that is to say, the Buddha’s qualities are produced from great causes, namely, the Buddha-making qualities known as perfections. Just as the great things like the earth and the great world-systems are each singular in their own domain, so too the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One is great and singular in his own domain. And what is his domain? The Buddha-ground, or as far as there is to be known. Saying, “Like space with its infinite domain, the Blessed One is singular,” he shows that even in other world-systems, there is no second Buddha.

Imināva padenāti “ekissā lokadhātuyā”ti iminā eva padena. Dasa cakkavāḷasahassāni gahitānīti jātikhettāpekkhāya gahitāni. Ekacakkavāḷenevāti iminā eva ekacakkavāḷena, na yena kenaci. Yathā “imasmiṃyeva cakkavāḷe uppajjantī”ti vutte imasmimpi cakkavāḷe jambudīpe eva, tatthāpi majjhimadese evāti paricchindituṃ vaṭṭati, evaṃ “ekissā lokadhātuyā”ti jātikhette adhippetepi imināva cakkavāḷena paricchindituṃ vaṭṭati.

'By this very phrase' refers to the phrase 'in one world-system.' The ten thousand world-systems are included with reference to the field of birth. 'By one world-system alone' means by this very one world-system, not by any other. Just as when it is said, “they arise in this very world-system,” it is proper to specify that this is in Jambudīpa within this world-system, and there too, in the Middle Country—so too, when 'in one world-system' is intended to refer to the field of birth, it is proper to specify it as this very world-system.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first section is concluded.

15. Aṭṭhānapāḷi (dutiyavagga)

15. The Text on Impossibilities (Second Section)

(15) 2. Aṭṭhānapāḷi-dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā

(15) 2. Commentary on the Second Section of the Text on Impossibilities

278. Vivādupacchedatoti [V 1.0205] vivādupacchedakāraṇā. Dvīsu uppannesu yo vivādo bhaveyya, tassa anuppādoyevettha vivādupacchedo. Ekasmiṃ dīpetiādinā dīpantarepi ekajjhaṃ na uppajjati, pageva ekadīpeti dasseti. Sopi parihāyethāti cakkavāḷassa padese eva pavattitabbattā parihāyeyya.

278. 'Vivādupacchedato' means for the reason of preventing disputes. When a dispute might arise between two who have arisen, the non-arising of that dispute is here the prevention of disputes. By 'in one island,' etc., it shows that they do not arise simultaneously even in different islands, let alone in one island. 'It would also diminish' means it would diminish since it must occur only in a region of the world-sphere.

279-280. Manussattanti [M 1.0220] manussabhāvo tasseva pabbajjādiguṇānaṃ yoggabhāvato. Liṅgasampattīti purisabhāvo. Hetūti manovacīpaṇidhānapubbikā hetusampadā. Satthāradassananti satthusammukhībhāvo. Pabbajjāti kammakiriyavādīsu tāpasesu, bhikkhūsu vā pabbajjā. Guṇasampattīti abhiññādiguṇasampadā. Adhikāroti buddhe uddissa adhiko kāro, savisesā upakārakiriyā adhiko sakkāroti vuttaṃ hoti. Chandova chandatā, sammāsambodhiṃ uddissa sātisayo kattukamyatākusalacchando. Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānāti etesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ dhammānaṃ samāyogena. Abhinīhāroti kāyapaṇidhānaṃ. Samijjhatīti nipphajjati. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana paramatthadīpaniyā cariyāpiṭakavaṇṇanāya (cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā) vuttanayena veditabbo. Sabbākāraparipūramevāti paripuṇṇalakkhaṇatāya sattuttamādīhi sabbākārena sampannameva. Na hi itthiyā kosohitavatthaguyhatādi sambhavati. Dutiyapakati ca nāma paṭhamapakatito nihīnā eva. Tenevāha – anantaravāre “yasmā”tiādi.

279-280. 'Manussattaṃ' means the human state, because of its suitability for qualities such as renunciation. 'Liṅgasampatti' means the male gender. 'Hetu' refers to the perfection of causes preceded by mental and verbal resolve. 'Satthāradassana' means being in the presence of the Teacher. 'Pabbajjā' refers to renunciation among ascetics who are adherents of karma and action, or among monks. 'Guṇasampatti' means the attainment of qualities such as the superknowledges. 'Adhikāra' means a great service dedicated to the Buddha; it is said to be a special act of assistance or superior honor. 'Chanda' is the state of wishing, an intense wholesome desire aspiring to perfect Buddhahood. 'Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānā' means by the combination of these eight qualities. 'Abhinīhāra' is bodily resolve. 'Samijjhati' means it is accomplished. This here is the summary; the detailed explanation should be understood according to the method stated in the Paramatthadīpanī, the commentary on the Cariyāpiṭaka (Cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā). 'Perfect in every way' means complete in all aspects, accomplished in every way through the perfection of characteristics, the seven superiorities, and so on. For it is not possible for a woman to have the male organ concealed in a sheath. And the second nature is indeed inferior to the first nature. Therefore, it is said in the immediately following passage: 'Because,' etc.

281. Idha purisassa tattha nibbattanatoti imasmiṃ manussaloke purisabhūtassa tattha brahmaloke brahmattabhāvena nibbattanato. Tena asatipi purisaliṅge purisākārā brahmāno hontīti dasseti. Taṃyeva ca purisākāraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ bhagavatā “yaṃ puriso brahmattaṃ kāreyyā”ti. Tenevāha – “samānepī”tiādi. Yadi evaṃ itthiyo brahmaloke na uppajjeyyunti āha – “brahmatta”ntiādi.

281. Here, 'for a male being born there' means for one who is a male in this human world, being born there in the Brahma-world in the state of being a Brahmā. Thus, it shows that even without the male organ, Brahmās have male forms. And it is with reference to that very male form that the Blessed One said, 'that a male might attain the state of a Brahmā.' Therefore, he said, 'even though,' etc. To the objection, 'If so, would women not be reborn in the Brahma-world?' he said: 'Brahmāhood,' etc.

290-295. “Kāyaduccaritassā”tiādipāḷiyā [V 1.0206] kammaniyāmo nāma kathito. Samañjanaṃ samaṅgo, samannāgamo, so etassa atthīti samaṅgī, samannāgato, samañjanasīlo vā samaṅgī, pubbabhāge upakaraṇasamudāyato pabhuti āyūhanavasena āyūhanasamaṅgītā, sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāvasena cetanāsamaṅgitā. Cetanāsantativasena vā āyūhanasamaṅgitā, taṃtaṃcetanākkhaṇavasena cetanāsamaṅgītā. Katūpacitassa avipakkavipākassa kammassa vasena kammasamaṅgitā. Kamme pana vipaccituṃ āraddhe vipākappavattivasena vipākasamaṅgitā. Kammādīnaṃ upaṭṭhānakālavasena upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā. Kusalākusalakammāyūhanakkhaṇeti kusalakammassa akusalakammassa [M 1.0221] ca samīhanakkhaṇe. Tathāti iminā kusalākusalakammapadaṃ ākaḍḍhati. Yathā kataṃ kammaṃ phaladānasamatthaṃ hoti, tathā kataṃ upacitaṃ. Vipākārahanti dutiyabhavādīsu vipaccanārahaṃ. Uppajjamānānaṃ upapattinimittaṃ upaṭṭhātīti yojanā. Upapattiyā uppajjanassa nimittaṃ kāraṇanti upapattinimittaṃ, kammaṃ, kammanimittaṃ, gatinimittañca. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana gatinimittavaseneva yojanā dassitā. Kammakammanimittānampi upaṭṭhānaṃ yathārahaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Yānissa tāni pubbe katāni kammāni, tānissa tasmiṃ samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhilambanti”ti (ma. ni. 3.248) vacanato sāyanhe mahantānaṃ pabbatakūṭānaṃ chāyā viya āsannamaraṇassa sattassa citte supine viya vipaccituṃ katokāsaṃ kammaṃ, tassa nimittaṃ gatinimittaṃ upatiṭṭhateva. Calatīti parivattati. Ekena hi kammunā tajje nimitte upaṭṭhite paccayavisesavasena tato aññena kammunā tadaññassa nimittassa upaṭṭhānaṃ parivattanaṃ. Sesā niccalā avasesā catubbidhāpi samaṅgitā niccalā aparivattanato.

290-295. By the Pāli passage beginning 'Regarding bodily misconduct,' the order of kamma has been explained. 'Samañjana' means connection or association; one who has this is 'samaṅgī'—connected, associated, or one whose nature it is to connect. From the initial stage of gathering the supporting conditions up to the moment of exertion, it is called 'exertion-connection' (āyūhanasamaṅgitā). By the determining volition, it is called 'volition-connection' (cetanāsamaṅgitā). Or, by the continuity of volition, it is 'exertion-connection'; by each volition-moment, it is 'volition-connection'. By kamma that has been done and accumulated but whose result has not yet ripened, it is 'kamma-connection' (kammasamaṅgitā). When the kamma begins to ripen, due to the arising of its result, it is 'result-connection' (vipākasamaṅgitā). By the time when kamma and so on present themselves, it is 'presentation-connection' (upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā). 'The moment of exerting wholesome or unwholesome kamma' refers to the moment of striving in wholesome or unwholesome kamma. By 'Thus,' the phrase 'wholesome and unwholesome kamma' is drawn in. Kamma done in such a way that it is capable of yielding fruit is what is meant by 'accumulated.' 'Ripe for result' means fit to ripen in a second existence and so on. 'For beings about to arise, the rebirth sign appears'—this is the construction. The sign of rebirth (upapattinimitta) is the sign, the cause, for arising in a rebirth; it is kamma, the sign of kamma, and the sign of destiny. In the commentary, however, the construction is shown only in terms of the sign of destiny. The presentation of kamma and the sign of kamma should also be understood as appropriate. As it is said: 'Whatever kammas they have done before, at that time, those kammas hang over them, loom over them, overhang them.' Just as in the evening the shadows of great mountain peaks loom, so too, for a being nearing death, the kamma that has found an opportunity to ripen, its sign, and the sign of destiny, certainly appear in the mind like a dream. 'Shifts' means it changes. For when, through one kamma, its corresponding sign has appeared, the appearance of a different sign through another kamma, due to a specific condition, is 'shifting.' The rest are unchanging—the remaining four kinds of connection are unchanging because they do not shift.

Sunakhavājikoti sunakhehi migavājavasena vajanasīlo, sunakhaluddakoti attho. Talasantharaṇapūjanti bhūmitalassa pupphehi santharaṇapūjaṃ. Āyūhanacetanā kammasamaṅgitāvasenāti kāyaduccaritassa aparāparaṃ āyūhanena sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāya tasseva pakappane kammakkhayakarañāṇena akhepitattā yathūpacitakammunā ca samaṅgibhāvassa vasena.

‘Sunakhavājika’ means one whose nature it is to go on a hunt with dogs, that is, a dog-hunter. ‘Talasantharaṇapūjā’ means the worship of spreading flowers on the ground surface. ‘The volition of accumulation, by way of connection with kamma’ means: by means of the state of being connected with the kamma as it was accumulated; because it was not cast off by the knowledge that destroys kamma; by the determining volition in the very establishing of it; and by the repeated accumulation of bodily misconduct.

Kammanti akusalakammaṃ. Tasmiṃyeva khaṇeti āyūhanakkhaṇeyeva. Tassāti kammasamaṅgino puggalassa saggo vārito, tañce kammaṃ vipākavāraṃ labheyyāti adhippāyo. Saggo vāritoti ca nidassanamattaṃ. Manussalokopissa vāritovāti. Apare pana purimehi vipākāvaraṇassa anuddhaṭattā “tasmiṃyeva khaṇe”ti ca avisesena vuttattā taṃ dosaṃ pariharituṃ “āyūhitakammaṃ nāmā”tiādimāha. Yadā kammaṃ vipākavāraṃ labhatīti idaṃ katokāsassa appaṭibāhiyattā vuttaṃ[V 1.0207]. Tathā hi bhagavā tatiyapārājikavatthusmiṃ (pārā. 162 ādayo) paṭisallīyi, imasmiṃ sutte “kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī”ti āgatattā vipākūpaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā na labbhanti.

‘Kamma’ means unwholesome kamma. ‘At that very moment’ means at the moment of exertion. ‘For him’ means for the person connected with that kamma, heaven is barred; the intention is, if that kamma were to get its turn to ripen. And ‘heaven is barred’ is merely an illustration. Even the human world is barred for him. Others, however, in order to avoid that fault—since the obstruction to the result was not removed by the preceding statements, and since ‘at that very moment’ was said without qualification—say, ‘It is called kamma that has been exerted,’ and so on. The statement that kamma gets its turn to ripen is said because one who has created an opportunity cannot be hindered. Indeed, the Blessed One was in seclusion regarding the story of the third pārājika. In this sutta, because the phrase ‘connected with bodily misconduct’ occurs, the ‘connection with the presentation of the result’ is not obtained.

(Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.)

(The commentary on the Second Chapter is finished.)

Aṭṭhānapāḷivaṇṇanāyaṃ anuttānatthadīpanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Unobvious Meaning in the Commentary on the Aṭṭhānapāḷi is finished.

16. Ekadhammapāḷi

16. The Pāli Text on Single Items

(16) 1. Ekadhammapāḷi-paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā

(16) 1. Commentary on the First Chapter of the Pāli Text on Single Items.

296. Ekadhammapāḷivaṇṇanāyaṃ [V 1.0208][M 1.0222] idha dhamma-saddo sabhāvattho “kusalā dhammā”tiādīsu viyāti āha – “ekasabhāvo”ti. Ekantenāti ekaṃsena, avassanti attho. Vaṭṭeti saṃsāravaṭṭe. Nibbindanatthāyāti anabhiramanatthāya. Virajjanatthāyāti arajjanatthāya. Virajjanāyāti palujjanāya. Tenevāha – “vigamāyā”ti. Rāgādīnaṃ nirodhāyāti maggañāṇena rāgādīnaṃ nirodhanatthāya. Maggañāṇena nirodhanaṃ nāma accantaṃ appavattikaraṇanti āha – “appavattikaraṇatthāyā”ti. Yathā khādanīyassa mukhe katvā khādanaṃ nāma yāvadeva ajjhoharaṇatthaṃ, evaṃ rāgādīnaṃ nirodhanaṃ vaṭṭanirodhanatthamevāti vuttaṃ – “vaṭṭasseva vā nirujjhanatthāyā”ti. Yasmā kilesesu khīṇesu itaraṃ vaṭṭadvayampi khīṇameva hoti, tasmā mūlameva gaṇhanto “upasamāyāti kilesavūpasamanatthāyā”ti āha. Saṅkhatadhammānaṃ abhijānanaṃ nāma tattha lakkhaṇattayāropanamukhenevāti āha – “aniccādi…pe… abhijānanatthāyā”ti. Sambujjhitabbāni nāma cattāri ariyasaccāni tabbinimuttassa ñeyyassa abhāvato. “Catunnaṃ saccānaṃ bujjhanatthāyā”ti vatvā tayidaṃ bujjhanaṃ yassa ñāṇassa vasena ijjhati, tassa ñāṇassa vasena dassetuṃ – “bodhi vuccatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Appaccayanibbānassāti amatadhātuyā.

296. In the commentary on the Pāli Text on Single Items, the word ‘dhamma’ here has the meaning of intrinsic nature, as in ‘wholesome dhammas’ and so on. Thus it is said: ‘one intrinsic nature.’ ‘Ekantena’ means decisively, that is, certainly. ‘Vaṭṭeti’ means in the cycle of saṃsāra. ‘Nibbindanatthāya’ means for the purpose of disenchantment. ‘Virajjanatthāya’ means for the purpose of dispassion. ‘Virajjanāya’ means for dissolution. Therefore, it is said: ‘for passing away.’ ‘For the cessation of lust and so on’ means for the purpose of the cessation of lust and so on by means of the knowledge of the path. Cessation by means of the knowledge of the path means making them absolutely not arise. Thus it is said: ‘for the purpose of preventing their arising.’ Just as putting food in the mouth and chewing is only for the purpose of swallowing, so too the cessation of lust and so on is solely for the purpose of the cessation of the cycle. Thus it is said: ‘or for the cessation of the cycle itself.’ Since when the defilements are destroyed, the other two cycles are also destroyed, therefore, taking the root, it is said: ‘for pacification,’ meaning for the pacification of defilements. The direct knowing of conditioned phenomena is by way of imposing the three characteristics upon them. Thus it is said: ‘for the direct knowing of impermanence, etc.’ The ‘things to be fully awakened to’ are the four noble truths, because there is no knowable object apart from them. Having stated, ‘for the awakening to the four truths,’ in order to show by means of which knowledge this awakening is accomplished, it is said: ‘enlightenment is called,’ and so on. ‘For the unconditioned Nibbāna’ means for the deathless element.

Ussāhajananatthanti kammaṭṭhāne abhiruciuppādanāya. Visakaṇṭakoti guḷassa vāṇijasamaññā. “Kismiñci dese desabhāsā”ti keci. Ucchuraso samapākapakko cuṇṇādīhi missetvā piṇḍīkato guḷo, apiṇḍīkato phāṇitaṃ. Pākavisesena khaṇḍakhaṇḍasedito khaṇḍo, malābhāvaṃ āpanno sakkarā.

‘For the purpose of arousing effort’ means for producing delight in the meditation subject. ‘Visakaṇṭaka’ is a merchant’s term for jaggery (guḷa). Some say: ‘In a certain country, it is the local language.’ Sugarcane juice, well-cooked, mixed with powders and so on, and made into a lump, is jaggery (guḷa); not made into a lump, it is molasses (phāṇita). By a special cooking process, broken into pieces, it becomes candy (khaṇḍa); having become free from impurities, it becomes sugar (sakkarā).

Saratīti sati. Anu anu saratīti anussati, anu anurūpā satītipi anussati. Duvidhaṃ hotīti payojanavasena duvidhaṃ hoti. Cittasampahaṃsanatthanti pasādanīyavatthusmiṃ pasāduppādanena bhāvanācittassa paritosanatthaṃ. Vipassanatthanti vipassanāsukhatthaṃ. Upacārasamādhinā hi citte samāhite vipassanāsukhena ijjhati. Cittuppādoti bhāvanāvasena pavatto cittuppādo[V 1.0209]. Upahaññati patihaññati paṭikūlattā ārammaṇassa. Tato [M 1.0223] eva ukkaṇṭhati, kammaṭṭhānaṃ riñcati, nirassādo hoti bhāvanassādassa alabbhanato. Pasīdati buddhaguṇānaṃ pasādanīyattā. Tathā ca kaṅkhādicetokhilābhāvena vinīvaraṇo hoti. Dametvāti nīvaraṇanirākaraṇena nibbisevanaṃ katvā. Evaṃ kammaṭṭhānantarānuyuñjanena cittaparidamanassa upamaṃ dassento, “katha”ntiādimāha.

‘Saratī’ means mindfulness (sati). ‘Anu anu saratī’ means recollection (anussati); mindfulness that is repeatedly appropriate (anu anurūpā sati) is also recollection. ‘It is twofold’ means it is twofold in terms of purpose. ‘Cittasampahaṃsanatthaṃ’ means for the purpose of gladdening the meditation mind by arousing serenity in a pleasing object. ‘Vipassanatthaṃ’ means for the sake of the happiness of insight. For when the mind is concentrated through access concentration, one succeeds with the happiness of insight. ‘Cittuppāda’ refers to the occurrence of a state of mind that proceeds by way of cultivation. ‘Upahaññati’ means it is afflicted, it is repelled, due to the disagreeable nature of the object. For that very reason, one becomes discontented, abandons the meditation subject, and becomes disenchanted, because the delight of cultivation is not obtained. One becomes serene, due to the pleasing nature of the Buddha's qualities. And thus, through the absence of doubt and other mental barrenness, one becomes free from the hindrances. ‘Dametvā’ means having tamed it by removing the hindrances, making it compliant. To illustrate the subduing of the mind by applying oneself continuously to another meditation subject, he then says, ‘How?’ and so forth.

Ko ayaṃ…pe… anussarīti ko ayaṃ mama abbhantare ṭhatvā anussari. Pariggaṇhantoti bāhirakaparikappitassa anussarakassa sabbaso abhāvadassanametaṃ. Tenāha – “na añño kocī”ti. Disvāti pariyesananayena vuttappakāraṃ cittameva anussarīti disvā sabbampetanti etaṃ hadayavatthuādippabhedaṃ sabbampi. Idañca rūpaṃ purimañca arūpanti idaṃ ruppanasabhāvattā rūpaṃ, purimaṃ ataṃsabhāvattā arūpanti saṅkhepato rūpārūpaṃ vavatthapetvā. Pañcakkhandhe vavatthapetvāti yojanā. Sambhāvikāti samuṭṭhāpikā. Tassāti samudayasaccassa. Nirodhoti nirodhanimittaṃ. Appanāvāroti yathāraddhāya desanāya nigamanavāro.

‘Who is this…pe… one who recollects?’ means: ‘Who is this that stands within me and recollects?’ ‘Pariggaṇhanto’ means showing the complete absence of any externally fabricated recollector. Therefore, it is said: ‘There is no other.’ ‘Disvā’ means having seen, by way of investigation, that the mind itself recollects in the manner described. ‘All of this’ means all of it, including the heart-base and other distinctions. ‘This form and the previous formless’ means that this is called form because it has the nature of being afflicted, while the previous is called formless because it lacks that nature. This is briefly distinguishing form and formless. The connection is: having distinguished the five aggregates. ‘Sambhāvikā’ means causative. ‘Of that’ refers to the truth of origin. ‘Nirodha’ is the sign of cessation. ‘Appanāvāra’ is the concluding section according to the teaching as it was begun.

297. Eseva nayoti iminā yvāyaṃ “taṃ paneta”ntiādinā atthanayo buddhānussatiyaṃ vibhāvitoti atidisati, svāyaṃ atideso payojanavasena navasupi anussatīsu sādhāraṇavasena vuttopi ānāpānassatiādīsu tīsu vipassanatthāneva hontīti iminā apavādena nivattitoti tāsaṃ ekappayojanatāva daṭṭhabbā. Dhamme anussati dhammānussatīti samāsapadavibhāgadassanampi vacanatthadassanapakkhikamevāti āha – “ayaṃ panettha vacanattho”ti. Dhammaṃ ārabbhāti hi dhammassa anussatiyā visayabhāvadassanametaṃ. Esa nayo sesesupi. Sīlaṃ ārabbhāti attano pārisuddhisīlaṃ ārabbha. Cāgaṃ ārabbhāti attano cāgaguṇaṃ ārabbha. Devatā ārabbhāti ettha devatāguṇasadisatāya attano saddhāsīlasutacāgapaññāsu devatāsamaññā. Bhavati hi taṃsadisepi tabbohāro yathā “tāni osadhāni, esa brahmadatto”ti ca. Tenāha – “devatā sakkhiṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā”tiādi. Tattha devatā sakkhiṭṭhāne ṭhapetvāti “yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṃvijjati. Yathārūpena sīlena, yathārūpena [M 1.0224] sutena, yathārūpena cāgena, yathārūpāya paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṃvijjatī”ti evaṃ devatā sakkhiṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā. Assāsapassāsanimittaṃ nāma tattha laddhabbappaṭibhāganimittaṃ. Gatāti ārammaṇakaraṇavasena upagatā pavattā.

297. ‘Eseva nayo’ (This is the method) means that the method of meaning clarified in the recollection of the Buddha by the phrase ‘taṃ paneta’ and so on, is thus applied by extension. Although this extension is stated generally for all nine recollections in terms of purpose, it is rescinded by the exception that the three recollections, such as mindfulness of breathing, are for the purpose of insight only. Therefore, it should be understood that they have a single purpose. The showing of the analysis of the compound word ‘dhammānussati’ as ‘Dhammaṃ anussati’ (recollection of the Dhamma) is also part of explaining the meaning of the term. Hence, it is said: ‘This is the meaning of the word here.’ ‘Dhammaṃ ārabbha’ shows that the Dhamma is the object of recollection. The same method applies to the others. ‘Sīlaṃ ārabbha’ refers to taking one’s own purified virtue as the object. ‘Cāgaṃ ārabbha’ refers to taking one’s own quality of generosity as the object. ‘Devatā ārabbha’ here refers to the designation ‘deity’ for one’s own faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, due to their similarity to the qualities of deities. For indeed, such a designation is used even for that which is similar, as in ‘Those are medicinal herbs,’ and ‘This is Brahmadatta.’ Therefore, it is stated: ‘Having established the deities in the position of witnesses,’ and so on. In this context, ‘having established the deities in the position of witnesses’ means: ‘Those deities who possessed such faith, having passed away from here, were reborn there; I too possess such faith. Those deities who possessed such virtue, such learning, such generosity, and such wisdom, having passed away from here, were reborn there; I too possess such virtue, such learning, such generosity, and such wisdom.’ Thus, having established the deities in the position of witnesses. ‘Assāsapassāsa-nimitta’ refers to the counterpart sign to be obtained in that context. ‘Gatā’ means that it has been approached and proceeds by being made an object.

Upasammati [V 1.0210] ettha dukkhanti upasamo, nibbānaṃ. Accantameva ettha upasammati vaṭṭattayanti accantūpasamo, nibbānameva. Khiṇoti khepeti kileseti khayo, ariyamaggo. Te eva upasametīti upasamo, ariyamaggo eva. Khayo ca so upasamo cāti khayūpasamo. Tatracāyaṃ upasamo dhammo evāti dhammānussatiyā upasamānussati ekasaṅgahoti? Saccaṃ ekasaṅgaho dhammabhāvasāmaññe adhippete, saṅkhatadhammato pana asaṅkhatadhammo sātisayo uḷāratamapaṇītatamabhāvatoti dīpetuṃ visuṃ nīharitvā vuttaṃ. Imameva hi visesaṃ sandhāya bhagavā – “dhammānussatī”ti vatvāpi upasamānussatiṃ avoca anussarantassa savisesaṃ santapaṇītabhāvena upaṭṭhānato. Evañca katvā idha khayūpasamaggahaṇampi samatthitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yatheva hi samānepi lokuttaradhammabhāve “yāvatā, bhikkhave, dhammā saṅkhatā vā asaṅkhatā vā, virāgo tesaṃ aggamakkhāyatī”tiādivacanato (itivu. 90) maggaphaladhammehi nibbānadhammo sātisayo, evaṃ phaladhammato maggadhammo kilesappahānena acchariyadhammabhāvato, tasmā accantūpasamena saddhiṃ khayūpasamopi gahitoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vipassanatthāneva hontīti kasmā vuttanti? “Ekantanibbidāyātiādivacanato”ti keci, taṃ akāraṇaṃ buddhānussatiādīsupi tathā desanāya āgatattā. Yathā pana buddhānussatiādīni kammaṭṭhānāni vipassanatthāni honti, nimittasampahaṃsanatthānipi honti, na evametāni, etāni pana vipassanatthānevāti tathā vuttaṃ.

Here suffering ceases: this is peace (upasama), Nibbāna. Here the round of existence ceases utterly: this is ultimate peace (accantūpasama), Nibbāna itself. It destroys, it makes an end: this is destruction (khaya), the Noble Path. They indeed pacify: this is peace (upasama), the Noble Path itself. Destruction and peace: this is the peace of destruction (khayūpasamo). Here, this peace is the Dhamma itself: thus, in the recollection of the Dhamma, is the recollection of peace included as one category? Indeed, it is one category when the common nature of being Dhamma is intended, but to highlight that, from the standpoint of conditioned phenomena, the unconditioned Dhamma is superior, being more sublime and more excellent, it is taught separately. For this very distinction, the Blessed One, after speaking of "recollection of the Dhamma," also taught the recollection of peace—because for one who recollects, it presents itself with its special qualities of calm and excellence. And thus, it should be understood that the inclusion of the peace of destruction here is also justified. Just as, even when the supramundane states are equal, from the statement, "Monks, as far as conditioned or unconditioned phenomena go, dispassion is declared the highest," etc., the Dhamma of Nibbāna is superior to the path and fruition Dhammas, so too the path Dhamma is superior to the fruition Dhamma by the marvelous nature of abandoning defilements. Therefore, the peace of destruction should be understood as included along with ultimate peace. Why is it said that these exist only for the purpose of insight? Some say it is because of the statement, "For the sake of complete disenchantment," but this is not the reason, since such instruction also applies to the recollections of the Buddha, etc. Just as the recollections of the Buddha, etc., are meditation subjects for insight and also for the purpose of gladdening the mind through the sign, these are not so. Rather, these are solely for the purpose of insight—thus it is said.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first chapter is concluded.

16. Ekadhammapāḷi

16. The Text on Single Phenomena

(16) 2. Ekadhammapāḷi-dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā

(16) 2. Commentary on the Second Chapter of the Ekadhamma Section

298. Micchā [V 1.0211] passati tāya, sayaṃ vā micchā passati, micchādassanameva vā tanti micchādiṭṭhi, yaṃ kiñci viparītadassanaṃ. Tenāha – “dvāsaṭṭhividhāyā”tiādi[M 1.0225]. Micchādiṭṭhi etassāti micchādiṭṭhiko. Tassa micchādiṭṭhikassa.

298. One sees wrongly through that, or one sees wrongly by oneself, or wrong seeing is indeed the system: this is wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), whatever seeing is contrary. Therefore, it is said: "of sixty-two kinds," and so on. Wrong view belongs to him: thus, one with wrong view (micchādiṭṭhiko). Of that one with wrong view.

299. Sammā passati tāya, sayaṃ vā sammā passati, sammādassanamattameva vā tanti sammādiṭṭhi. Pañcavidhāyāti kammassakatājhānavipassanāmaggaphalavasena pañcavidhāya. Tattha jhānacittuppādapariyāpannaṃ ñāṇaṃ jhānasammādiṭṭhi, vipassanāñāṇaṃ vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi.

299. One sees rightly through that, or one sees rightly by oneself, or merely right seeing is the system: this is right view (sammādiṭṭhi). It is fivefold: by way of ownership of kamma, jhāna, insight, path, and fruition. Here, the knowledge included in the occurrence of jhāna consciousness is jhāna right view, and the knowledge of insight is insight right view.

302. Pañcasu khandhesu “nicca”ntiādinā pavatto anupāyamanasikāro.

302. Unwise attention that proceeds in the five aggregates with notions such as "permanent," and so on.

303. “Anicca”ntiādinā pavatto upāyamanasikāro. Yāva niyāmokkamanāti yāva micchattaniyāmokkamanā. Micchattaniyāmokkamananayo pana sāmaññaphalasuttavaṇṇanāyaṃ taṭṭīkāya ca vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

303. Wise attention that proceeds with notions such as "impermanent," and so on. Up to the emergence from the fixed course—that is, up to the emergence from the fixed course of wrongness. The method of emerging from the fixed course of wrongness should be understood according to the explanation given in the commentary on the Sāmaññaphala Sutta and in its subcommentary.

304. Ayaṃ tividhā saggāvaraṇā ceva hotīti kammapathappattiyā mahāsāvajjabhāvato vuttaṃ. Saggāvaraṇāya hontiyā maggavibandhakabhāve vattabbameva natthīti vuttaṃ – “maggāvaraṇā cā”ti. “Sassato loko”tiādikā dasavatthukā antaggāhikā micchādiṭṭhi. Maggāvaraṇāva hoti viparītadassanabhāvato, na saggāvaraṇā akammapathapattitoti adhippāyo. Idaṃ pana vidhānaṃ paṭikkhipitvāti viparītadassanañca na maggāvaraṇañcāti viruddhametaṃ uddhammabhāvato. Tathā hi sati appahīnāya eva sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā maggādhigamena bhavitabbanti adhippāyena yathāvuttavidhānaṃ paṭikkhipitvā. “Na saggāvaraṇā”ti saggūpapattiyā avibandhakattaṃ vadantehi diṭṭhiyā saggāvahatāpi nāma anuññātā hotīti taṃ vādaṃ paṭikkhipantena “diṭṭhi nāma saggaṃ upanetuṃ samatthā nāma natthī”ti vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Ekantagarutarasāvajjabhāvato. Tenāha – “ekantaṃ nirayasmiṃyeva nimujjāpetī”tiādi.

304. These three are indeed obstacles to heaven—this is said because they are grave offenses due to having reached the level of a course of action. When they are obstacles to heaven, there is no need to mention that they are obstacles to the path—hence it is said, 'and obstacles to the path.' The tenfold wrong view that grasps at extremes, such as 'the world is eternal,' is an obstacle to the path because it is a distorted view; it is not an obstacle to heaven because it does not reach the level of a course of action—this is the intended meaning. But to reject this explanation, saying that a distorted view is not an obstacle to the path, is contradictory, for it is against the true Dhamma. For if that were so, it would mean that the path could be attained even with identity view not abandoned. Rejecting the aforementioned explanation with this intention... By those who say, 'it is not an obstacle to heaven,' claiming it does not obstruct rebirth in heaven, they in effect permit that a view can lead to heaven. Refuting that argument, it is stated: 'A view is indeed not capable of leading to heaven.' Why? Because it is an offense of the most serious gravity. Hence it is said: 'It plunges one entirely into hell,' and so on.

305. Vaṭṭaṃ [V 1.0212] viddhaṃsetīti maggasammādiṭṭhi kilesavaṭṭaṃ kammavaṭṭañca viddhaṃseti. Vipākavaṭṭaṃ kā nu viddhaṃseti nāma. Evaṃ pana attano kāraṇena viddhastabhavaṃ phalasammādiṭṭhi paṭibāhatīti vuttaṃ avasaradānato. Iccetaṃ kusalanti arahattaṃ pāpetuṃ sace sakkoti, evametaṃ vipassanāya paṭisandhianākaḍḍhanaṃ [M 1.0226] kusalaṃ anavajjaṃ. Satta bhave detīti sotāpattimaggassa paccayabhūtā vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi tassa puggalassa satta bhave deti. Evamayanti pañcavidhampi sammādiṭṭhiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha – “lokiyalokuttarā sammādiṭṭhi kathitā”ti. Imasmiṃ panattheti “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmī”tiādinā vutte gatimaggasaṅkhāte atthe. “Sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti vuttattā “lokikā bhavanipphādikāva veditabbā”ti vuttaṃ.

305. 'It shatters the cycle'—right view of the path shatters the cycle of defilements and the cycle of kamma. But what, indeed, shatters the cycle of results? However, it is said that right view of fruition, by not giving an opportunity, wards off the existence shattered by its own cause. 'This is wholesome'—if it is able to lead to arahantship, then this wholesome and blameless insight does not draw one toward rebirth. 'It grants seven existences'—the right view of insight, which is a condition for the path of stream-entry, grants that person seven existences. Thus, this is said with reference to the fivefold right view. Hence it is said: 'Mundane and supramundane right view have been explained.' In this context—in the sense of what is called the path to a destination, spoken of in the text beginning, 'Monks, I do not see even one other thing...' Since it is said, 'They are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world,' it is said that it should be understood as the mundane right view which produces existence.

306. Yathādiṭṭhīti atthabyāpanicchāyaṃ yathā-saddo, tena uttarapadatthappadhāno samāsoti āha – “yā yā diṭṭhī”ti. Tassā tassā anurūpanti taṃtaṃdiṭṭhianurūpanti attho. Samattanti anavasesaṃ. Tenāha – “paripuṇṇa”nti. Samādinnanti ādimajjhapariyosānesu samaṃ ekasadisaṃ katvā ādinnaṃ gahitaṃ anissaṭṭhaṃ. Tadetanti yadetaṃ “yañceva kāyakamma”ntiādinā vuttaṃ, tadetaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Yathādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitakāyakammanti yā pana diṭṭhi “natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpa”ntiādinā pavattā, tassaṃ diṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitakassa ṭhitamattassa anissaṭṭhassa taṃdiṭṭhikassa kāyakammaṃ. Diṭṭhisahajātaṃ kāyakammanti tassa yathādiṭṭhikassa paresaṃ hatthamuddādinā viññāpanakāle tāya diṭṭhiyā sahajātaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Na cettha vacīkammāsaṅkā uppādetabbā pāṇaghātādīnaṃyeva adhippetattā. Diṭṭhānulomikaṃ kāyakammanti yathā paresaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, evaṃ diṭṭhiyā anulomikaṃ katvā pavattitaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Tenāha – “samādinnaṃ gahitaṃ parāmaṭṭha”nti. Tatthātiādi suviññeyyameva. Eseva nayoti iminā yathāvuttāya diṭṭhiyā ṭhitavacīkammaṃ, diṭṭhisahajātaṃ vacīkammaṃ, diṭṭhānulomikaṃ vacīkammanti tividhaṃ hotīti evamādi atidisati. Micchādiṭṭhikassāti kammapathappattāya micchādiṭṭhiyā micchādiṭṭhikassa. “Yāya kāyaci micchādiṭṭhiyā micchādiṭṭhikassa sato”ti apare.

306. Regarding 'yathādiṭṭhī': the word 'yathā' is used for clarifying the meaning, and therefore it is a compound where the meaning of the latter part is predominant. Hence he said: 'whatever view.' 'Tassā tassā anurūpanti' means corresponding to each respective view. 'Samattanti' means without remainder. Therefore, it is said: 'fully.' 'Samādinnanti' means taken up, grasped, and not abandoned, having been made equal and uniform in the beginning, middle, and end. 'Tadetanti' refers to what is stated by 'whatever bodily action,' and so on—that very bodily action. 'Yathādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitakāyakammaṃ' means the bodily action of one who is established in a view such as 'there is no evil arising from this,' and so on—that is, the bodily action of one holding that view, who is merely established in it and has not abandoned it. 'Diṭṭhisahajātaṃ kāyakammaṃ' refers to the bodily action of one holding such a view that co-arises with that view at the time of communicating to others by hand gestures and so on. Here, the possibility of verbal action should not be raised, because only actions like killing living beings and so on are intended. 'Diṭṭhānulomikaṃ kāyakammaṃ' means bodily action performed in conformity with the view, so that it becomes manifest to others. Therefore, it is said: 'taken up, grasped, and adhered to.' 'Tatthātiādi' is easily understood. 'Eseva nayo'—by this he extends the application, saying that verbal action is also threefold: verbal action of one established in the aforementioned view, verbal action co-arising with the view, and verbal action conforming to the view, and so on. 'Micchādiṭṭhikassāti' means of one with the wrong view that has reached the level of a course of action. Others say: 'of one who has whatever wrong view.'

Diṭṭhisahajātāti yathāvuttāya diṭṭhiyā sahajātā cetanā. Esa nayo sesapadesupi. Patthanāti “idaṃ nāma kareyya”nti taṇhāpatthanā. Cetanāpatthanānaṃ vasenāti yathāvuttadiṭṭhigatanissitacetasikanikāmanānaṃ vasena. Cittaṭṭhapanāti cittassa paṇidahanā. Phassādayoti cetanādiṭṭhitaṇhādivinimuttā phassādidhammā. Yasmā diṭṭhi pāpikā, tasmā tassa puggalassa sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya…pe… saṃvattantīti yojanā. Purimassevāti [M 1.0227] tittakapadasseva[V 1.0213]. Tittakaṃ kaṭukanti ca ubhayaṃ idha aniṭṭhapariyāyaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ “pacchā te kaṭukaṃ bhavissatī”tiādīsu viya.

'Co-arisen with the view' means the volition that is co-arisen with the aforementioned view. This is the method for the remaining terms as well. 'Aspiration' is the aspiration of craving, 'May I do this.' 'By the power of volition and aspiration' means by the power of the mental desires based on the aforementioned view. 'Fixing of the mind' is the directing of the mind. 'Contact and so forth' refers to phenomena such as contact, etc., that are distinct from volition, view, craving, and so on. The connection is: 'Because the view is evil, therefore all those phenomena for that person conduce to what is undesirable...' 'Of the former' means of the word 'bitter.' Both 'bitter' and 'acrid' should be seen here as synonyms for 'undesirable,' as in phrases like 'later it will be acrid for you,' and so on.

Amboyanti ambo ayaṃ. Tameva pūjanti tameva pubbe laddhaparisiñcanadānādipūjaṃ. Nivesareti pavisiṃsu. Asātasannivāsenāti amadhuranimbamūlasaṃsaggena.

'Amboyanti' means 'this is a mango tree.' 'They worship only that' refers to only that worship previously received, such as the offering of sprinkling, gifts, and so on. 'Nivesareti' means 'they entered.' 'Asātasannivāsena' means by contact with the bitter neem root.

Taṃ pana paṭikkhipitvā…pe… vuttanti sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi ekantasāvajjattā aniṭṭhāya dukkhāya saṃvattatīti adhippāyena vuttaṃ. Anantarasutteti dasamasutte. Yojetvā veditabbānīti navamasutte viya yojetvā veditabbāni. Cittaṭṭhapanāva patthanāti ettha paṇidhi cāti vattabbaṃ.

'But having rejected that... it is said'—it is said with the intention that all wrong view, being entirely blameworthy, conduces to what is undesirable and to suffering. 'In the immediately following sutta' means in the tenth sutta. 'They should be understood by connecting them' means they should be understood by connecting them as in the ninth sutta. 'Fixing of the mind is aspiration'; here, 'and resolve' should also be stated.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Second Chapter is concluded.

16. Ekadhammapāḷi

16. The Text on a Single Thing

(16) 3. Ekadhammapāḷi-tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā

(16) 3. Commentary on the Third Chapter of the Text on a Single Thing

308. Tatiyassa [V 1.0214] paṭhame ayāthāvadiṭṭhikoti aniccādibhāvesu dhammesu niccātiādinā uppannadiṭṭhiko. Tenāha – “tāyeva micchādiṭṭhiyā viparītadassano”ti saddhammāti ettha santo pasattho sundaro dhammo, yo manussadhammotipi vuccati. Tato hi micchādiṭṭhiko paraṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, na ariyadhammato. Tenāha – “dasakusalakammapathadhammato”ti. Evarūpāti iminā pāthikaputtādike saṅgaṇhāti.

308. In the first sutta of the third chapter, 'one with an incorrect view' means one in whom the view has arisen that phenomena which are impermanent, etc., are permanent, etc. Hence he said: 'one with a distorted view due to that very wrong view.' Here, 'true Dhamma' is the good, praiseworthy, and beautiful Dhamma, which is also called the human Dhamma. For one with wrong view would cause another to deviate from that, not from the noble Dhamma. Hence he said: 'from the Dhamma of the tenfold path of wholesome actions.' 'Of such a kind'—by this he includes Pāthikaputta and others.

309. Sabbaññubodhisattoti sabbaññubhāgī bodhisatto. Ādi-saddena pūritapāramikā paccekabodhisattā ekaccasāvakabodhisattā ca saṅgayhanti.

309. 'An omniscient Bodhisatta' is a Bodhisatta who partakes in omniscience. By the word 'ādi,' Paccekabodhisattas who have fulfilled the perfections and certain disciple-Bodhisattas are included.

310. Paramāti mahāsāvajjabhāvena paramā, ukkaṃsagatāti attho. Tesanti ānantariyakammānaṃ. Paricchedoti vipākavasena pariyosānaṃ. Vaṭṭassa mūlaṃ, tato taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo vaṭṭassa khāṇūti vuccati. Tenāha – “tāyā”tiādi. Tañce gāhaṃ na vissajjeti, tassa punapi tabbhāvāvahattā vuttaṃ – “bhavato vuṭṭhānaṃ natthī”ti, na pana sabbaso vuṭṭhānassa abhāvato. Yādise hi paccaye paṭicca ayaṃ taṃ dassanaṃ okkanto puna kadāci tappaṭipakkhe paccaye paṭicca tato sīsukkhipanamassa na hotīti na [M 1.0228] vattabbaṃ. Akusalañhi nāmetaṃ abalaṃ dubbalaṃ, na kusalaṃ viya mahābalaṃ. Aññathā sammattaniyāmo viya micchattaniyāmopi accantiko siyā, na ca micchattaniyāmo accantiko. Teneva papañcasūdaniyaṃ (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.100) –

310. “Paramā” means supreme, due to its great blameworthiness, that is, being of the highest degree. “Tesaṃ” refers to the ānantariya kammas. “Paricchedo” means the limit in terms of result. It is the root of the cycle of existence, and therefore an individual possessing such qualities is called the stump of the cycle. Therefore, it is said: “tāyā” and so on. If one does not abandon that grasping, because it leads again to that state, it is said: “There is no emergence from existence,” but not that there is a complete absence of emergence. For, depending on whatever conditions this person has entered upon that view, it cannot be said that, when opposing conditions arise, there will never be for him a raising of the head from it. Indeed, this unwholesome is weak and feeble, not like the wholesome, which is very strong. Otherwise, just as the fixed course of rightness, the fixed course of wrongness too might be absolute, but the fixed course of wrongness is not absolute. Therefore, in the Papañcasūdanī (Majjhima Nikāya Commentary 2.100),

“Kiṃ panesa ekasmiṃyeva attabhāve niyato hoti, udāhu aññasmimpīti? Ekasmiṃyeva niyato, āsevanavasena bhavantarepi taṃ diṭṭhiṃ roceti evā”ti –

“What then, is this person fixed in just one existence, or also in another? He is fixed in just one existence, but due to habitual cultivation, he approves of that view in another existence as well.”

Vuttaṃ. Tatoyeva ca sumaṅgalavilāsiniyampi (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.170-172) vuttaṃ –

It is said. And for that very reason, in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī (Dīgha Nikāya Commentary 1.170-172) it is also said –

“Ye [V 1.0215] vā pana tesaṃ laddhiṃ gahetvā rattiṭṭhāne divāṭṭhāne nisinnā sajjhāyanti vīmaṃsanti, tesaṃ ‘karoto na karīyati pāpaṃ, natthi hetu, natthi paccayo, mato ucchijjatī’ti tasmiṃ ārammaṇe micchāsati santiṭṭhati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, javanāni javanti. Paṭhamajavane satekicchā honti, tathā dutiyādīsu. Sattame buddhānampi atekicchā anivattino ariṭṭhakaṇṭakasadisā, tattha koci ekaṃ dassanaṃ okkamati, koci dve, koci tīṇipi, ekasmiṃ okkantepi dvīsu tīsu okkantesupi niyatamicchādiṭṭhikova hoti. Patto saggamaggāvaraṇañceva mokkhamaggāvaraṇañca, abhabbo tassattabhāvassa anantaraṃ saggampi gantuṃ, pageva mokkhaṃ, vaṭṭakhāṇu nāmesa satto pathavigopako, yebhuyyena evarūpassa bhavato vuṭṭhānaṃ natthī”ti.
